items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent years, sentiment analysis has been widely applied in various fields such as smart home, intelligent healthcare, and education. Multiple technologies such as eye movement recognition and text analysis are employed as means to determine the emotional state of users. However, during this process, factors such as sensor failures, privacy restrictions, and environmental disturbances can all lead to the problem of modal absence in sentiment analysis. Traditional multimodal approaches often fail to handle the correlations between different modalities during feature extraction, and when integrating features, they often neglect multi-scale emotional cues. This research aims to summarize typical multimodal feature fusion models. Based on four optimized models developed in recent years, it aims to summarize and outline the technical breakthroughs in the emerging model architectures in addressing the issue of modality absence in multimodal sentiment analysis, and also makes assumptions and prospects for future multimodal sentiment analysis in dealing with modality absence.</jats:p>
title: Modalities Missing in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) has become a crucial component of affective computing and multimodal video understanding, yet its reliability in real-world applications is severely compromised by inevitable data corruption and missing modalities (e.g., visual occlusion or frame loss). Current approaches exhibit limited cross-modal interaction, struggle to fully capture hierarchical dependencies, and often employ simplistic integrations of global and local features. Furthermore, conventional unified reconstruction strategies may cause irreversible semantic loss, significantly degrading model robustness under modality-deficient conditions. To address these critical challenges, we propose a novel framework: the Hierarchical Cross-Modal Transformer with Differentiated Modality Reconstruction (HCT-DMR). First, the HCT achieves deep fusion of multimodal features through a synergistic mechanism of hierarchical interaction and global semantic integration, effectively bridging modality gaps. Second, the DMR module applies mathematical constraints tailored to the distinct statistical distributions of text, audio, and video modalities (e.g., non-negative constraints for visual facial action units). This guarantees that the reconstructed features strictly align with their original semantic spaces, preventing representation degradation. Additionally, we introduce an Enhanced Temporal Encoding Architecture (ETEA) to strengthen non-verbal feature representation in complex temporal environments. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets (CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS) demonstrate that HCT-DMR establishes state-of-the-art robustness, providing a highly reliable sentiment prediction framework for complex, modality-deficient visual-linguistic scenarios.</jats:p>
title: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis under Missing Modalities via Hierarchical Interaction and Differentiated Reconstruction
